curated.instructions: omr/instructions/42000-1-1.pdf, 42000-1-2.pdf, 42000-1-3.pdf (all three books build the racer; book 3 pages 43-46 are the optional Power Functions add-on, 8293, which the model file doesn't include)

functions.does: The steering wheel in the cockpit steers the front wheels: its column runs forward under the nose through bevel gears to a gear on the steering rack, which pushes the track rods out to both front uprights.
functions.source: book 2 and 3: the steering column and front axle; inferred: the book draws no arrow for steering

functions.does: Rolling the car turns the V8 engine: the rear wheels drive a differential through two half-shafts with CV joints, and the differential turns the crankshaft, so the eight pistons go up and down.
functions.source: book 1: steps 1-17 (differential and rear end), book 2: engine; inferred: the engine is the rear wheels' only load, so it's driven as in every Technic car of the time
functions.note: through the differential: turning one rear wheel with the other held turns the engine at half speed; the pistons slide in fixed cylinders

functions.does: The black knob on the side behind the cockpit, with the yellow selector lever above it, works two things: with the lever one way, the knob tilts the rear wing's upper flap (a small linear actuator behind the engine pushes it); with the lever the other way, it lifts the whole engine cover, raised by two small linear actuators beside the engine.
functions.source: book 1: steps 4-12 (the gearbox with driving ring and the yellow lever); book 3: step 104 (the yellow arrows on the lever, knob and wing); function page book 3 p42 (insets 1 and 2)
functions.note: the selector lever is p251 32526, which slides the change-over catch p246 6641 and the driving ring p155 6539 between the clutch gears p156 6542b and p177 6542b; which lever position gives which function isn't stated plainly, and the engine cover's own parts weren't pinned down

functions.does: Each front wheel rides on double wishbones with a pushrod to a rocker inside the nose, which works a shock absorber lying across the car (pushrod suspension).
functions.source: book 2 and 3: front suspension; inferred: no motion arrows

functions.does: Each rear wheel rides on double wishbones with a pushrod to a rocker above the gearbox, which works a shock absorber (pushrod suspension).
functions.source: book 2: rear suspension; inferred: no motion arrows

functions.does: The shock absorbers' springs hold the car up on its suspension.
functions.skip: the springs only push back under the model's weight

questions.question: Which way does each lever go for which function? The `first` amounts in this file are guesses.
